meta.title: Four Generations from Taoyuan: family data
meta.source: Two family accounts written down by the fourth generation, September 2026. Names of people, the home village, the college, and the steel plant are withheld or pseudonymous.
meta.approximate_rule: Fields marked approx are estimates placed for mapping; the family account gives no exact year.

moves.label: Fleeing to Cili
moves.text: In 1945 the family flees west to Cili County for about six months, leaving its property behind.

moves.label: Back to Taoyuan
moves.text: After about half a year they come home, and the eldest son goes back to private school in the village.

moves.label: Taoyuan to Changde
moves.text: The year the family's property is confiscated, the eldest son finishes primary school and goes to middle school in Changde.

moves.label: Changde to Wuhan
moves.text: At sixteen he is admitted to an engineering college in Wuhan to study construction engineering.

moves.label: Taoyuan to Changsha
moves.text: The eldest daughter leaves home alone to study in Changsha and settles there. Year not recorded.

moves.label: Wuhan to Ezhou
moves.text: After graduating he joins a steel plant in Ezhou as a technician, and stays for forty-one years.

moves.label: Village to town
moves.text: Early 1980s. Part of the property is returned and the family moves from the village into the local town.

moves.label: Ezhou to Wuhan
moves.text: The third generation moves to Wuhan and settles there.

moves.label: Wuhan to Montreal
moves.text: The fourth generation goes abroad to study.

events.label: End of the empire
events.text: The Xinhai Revolution ends the Qing dynasty; the Republic of China is founded in 1912.

events.label: War against Japan
events.text: Fighting reaches Changde, the prefecture that includes Taoyuan, in 1943. Many families flee west into the mountains.

events.label: Battle of West Hunan
events.text: Japan's last major offensive in Hunan is fought in the west of the province from April to June 1945.

events.label: Liberation of Changde and Taoyuan
events.text: The People's Republic is founded in October 1949. The counties around Changde, Taoyuan among them, come under the new government between mid-July and early August 1949.

events.label: Rent and interest reduction
events.text: Before land redistribution, rents and loan interest owed to landlords are cut.

events.label: Land reform
events.text: Hunan's land reform runs from the winter of 1950 to the spring of 1952. Land is redistributed and every rural household receives a class label.

events.label: First Five-Year Plan
events.text: State-led heavy industry. Wuhan becomes a major base for steel and construction; the Wuhan Yangtze River Bridge opens in 1957.

events.label: Household registration rules
events.text: The 1958 hukou regulations fix each person as rural or urban and sharply limit moves from countryside to city.

events.label: People's communes
events.text: Rural land and labour are organized into collectives until the early 1980s.

events.label: Cultural Revolution
events.text: Families with a landlord label remain under political pressure.

events.label: University entrance exam returns
events.text: The national gaokao is restored after eleven years.

events.label: Reform and opening
events.text: Market reforms begin; the economy starts decades of fast growth.

events.label: Rural reform and restitution
events.text: Collectives give way to household farming, and restitution policies return some confiscated property.

events.label: Housing reform
events.text: Work-unit housing ends; city homes become purchases, usually with a mortgage.

events.label: University expansion
events.text: University enrolment expands rapidly.

events.label: WTO accession
events.text: China joins the World Trade Organization.

events.label: Urban majority
events.text: For the first time, more than half of China's population lives in cities.

events.label: Li Hanqing born
events.text: Born in the countryside of Taoyuan County.

events.label: Estate grows
events.text: With higher education and his parents' savings, he expands the family farmland; the household becomes a known landlord family.

events.label: Li Zhiyuan born
events.text: The eldest son is born in the home village, in the middle of the war.

events.label: Private school
events.text: At five, the eldest son starts at a private school in the home village.

events.label: Six months as refugees
events.text: The family flees to Cili County for about half a year, leaving its property behind.

events.label: Home again
events.text: Back in Taoyuan, the family runs its property again and the eldest son returns to private school, then primary school.

events.label: Confiscation and imprisonment
events.text: Land reform reaches the family. The property is confiscated, the household is left bankrupt, and Li Hanqing is imprisoned. His son finishes primary school and leaves for middle school in Changde.

events.label: College, and release
events.text: The eldest son, sixteen, enters an engineering college in Wuhan. The same year his father is released from prison and returned to Taoyuan for three years of labour reform.

events.label: Eldest daughter to Changsha
events.text: The eldest daughter leaves to study in Changsha. The four younger siblings stay and farm.

events.label: Forty-one years in steel
events.text: Li Zhiyuan joins a steel plant in Ezhou as a technician and rises to senior engineer in building design, construction, and management, retiring in 2000.

events.label: Eighteen years of silence
events.text: Because of his father's history, Li Zhiyuan cuts off contact with his family in Taoyuan. They do not speak again until 1981.

events.label: Third generation born
events.text: The eldest son's children are born in Ezhou.

events.label: Status restored, contact resumed
events.text: Li Hanqing's status is restored and he retires. His son reconnects with the family after eighteen years.

events.label: Property partly returned
events.text: Part of the property is returned and the family moves into the local town.

events.label: Ezhou to Wuhan
events.text: The third generation moves to the provincial capital and settles there.

events.label: Urban middle class
events.text: The third generation's careers grow with the economy in Wuhan.

events.label: Study abroad
events.text: With family support, the fourth generation studies in Canada.
